name: GGBench (gg-bench)
description: GGBench is a collection of 126 synthetically generated two-player game environments (filtered from 1,000) designed to evaluate general reasoning and strategic decision-making in LLMs. Models are prompted with a novel game's natural-language rules, the current board state, and the list of valid moves, then must select an action; they are scored by win rate against reinforcement learning agents trained via self-play (PPO) on each game. Because the benchmark is a data-generating process rather than a fixed dataset, new games can be produced on demand, making it structurally resistant to contamination. Reasoning models (o1, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1) achieve ~31–36% win rate, while standard instruction-tuned models score only 7–9%, revealing a sharp capability gap.
evaluation_method: win_rate against PPO-trained RL agents (30 games per environment)
general_score_metric: average win rate across all 126 games
reputation: May 2025 preprint from UC Berkeley; notable for exposing a 4× gap between reasoning and non-reasoning frontier models and for being a contamination-resistant generative benchmark.
notes: 126 games survived multi-stage filtering from an initial pool of 1,000 generated games. Five categories: number games (36.7%), board games (27.6%), card games (14.6%), chance games (11.7%), combat games (9.4%). Generation pipeline cost ~$1,162 using OpenAI o1. Each model plays 30 games per environment (win rates reported with 95% CIs). GitHub: github.com/vivek3141/gg-bench. arXiv: 2505.07215. License: MIT.
